tweets.text:
Be careful chasing coins tied to narratives that are dependent on news and headlines.

e.g. have seen a lot of people chasing GTA VI coins

one of the most popular narratives has been what the name of the in game currency will be

the issue with this type of narrative is - the in game currency will have NOTHING to do with any of the memes being made about it...

the only people who will initially be interested in stacking a meme about it instead of stacking the actual in game currency itself are already trading it

could a winner eventually pick up more steam as the trenches as a whole pick back up?

sure!

but odds are - most events like this in this type of market end up being sell the news and require a decent amount of distribution and time before they continue to send higher

if you're fine with that and want to try and nail the exact top of the narrative, no worries

gl & godspeed

tweets.text:
Honest take on the AI Nuremberg trailer from someone who has been pretty resistant to AI film

The Good:
+ Amazing imagery, worldbuilding and translation of the lore, if you know it
+ Insane 1 person can do this and the visual/audio editing makes me hyped for the film, first time feeling that
+ Huge reduction in cost compared to previous tech (CGI etc) to render and create entire new worlds, even if all film doesn't go this way, a new industry will be born around it
+ the marvel/netflix-ification of cinema means we've already got a ton of human made slop that is no better than this now. So complaints purely directed at it being derivative fall flat
+ This still needed someone who knew the lore, picked the shots and timed the edit. That's the impressive part
+ Overall insane how far we've come from Will Smith eating spaghetti

The Less Good/Skeptical:
- A lot of what makes it work is lifted from recent films (1917 visual, boots from 28 years later) which is closer to a collage than inspiring something new. Whether AI can ever truly do that is another question*
- It's a trailer. Mapping that out into a film that not only makes sense but is engaging is infinitely harder and a different skillset
- Most complaints about AI content are dialogue and characters. It's hard to judge that as there is none of that here. Ultimately it's what films live or die on

Overall I'm super impressed. Especially given the speed of the improvement in AI, but it's worth pointing out that is all it is for now - a trailer, and the parts missing are exactly where AI has been weakest so far

I will see it if it's made. Out of sheer curiosity if nothing else. Which says a lot about how far it's come
